brief: GS's cross-asset wrap ties the US midterms to two market moves: anti-AI regulation risk is expected to slow data-center CapEx, while deep unpopularity of the Iran war has eroded oil's risk premium, with markets pricing an accelerated end to the conflict. Physical Brent now trades near $94 (down ~$8.50 on the session) at a record $2.87 discount to Dated Brent, versus a >$20/bl discount three weeks ago, which the author reads as supportive for rates and consumer and as flipping gold into an inverse-oil trade as EM reserve managers stop tapping gold to cover energy bills. In equities, VIX fell 20% to 16.61 and VXN 18% to 25.08 as hyperscalers, quality and defensives led; the author calls this rotation, not liquidation, with nets and hedges already low. European tech flows turned bearish, with chips-to-infrastructure selling on legislative-restriction fears, which the author argues risks an inventory cycle (not demand destruction) at ASML/TSMC, while existing compute owners like Amazon benefit from capacity scarcity. Politically, Trump's openness to working with Democrats and betting markets favoring moderate 2028 candidates support a regulation-pivots-not-moratorium read, keeping the broader equity backdrop constructive even with AI sidelined.
